group.name: Independent GPU mode (opt-in; read the requirements first)

plugin.name: I use Community Shaders or ReShade (Warning — read description)
plugin.description:
Use this option if Community Shaders (including Bottled/Open Shaders), ReShade or another graphics mod causes problems with the default shared GPU mode.
What does this do? BFA creates a separate software connection to your graphics card for facial-animation processing. This DirectX feature is called "Independent Devices". Skyrim and BFA still use the same physical graphics card; you do not need a second card.
Requirements — follow the section for your operating system:
WINDOWS Install the August 22, 2023 cumulative Windows update or a later cumulative update: • Windows 10 22H2: KB5029331 (OS build 19045.3393). • Windows 11 21H2: KB5029332 (OS build 22000.2360). • Windows 11 22H2: KB5029351 (OS build 22621.2215). Newer Windows 11 versions already include this Windows feature. You do not need to install these old updates if you have a newer cumulative update or Windows version. Run winver from the Start menu to check your version and build.
LINUX / PROTON Use a Proton build whose included vkd3d-proton supports Independent Devices. The Windows updates listed above are only for people running Windows.
ON EITHER SYSTEM Your graphics driver must also support this feature. Install the latest driver available for your graphics card. Having DirectX 12 alone does not guarantee support.
If a requirement is missing, the model does not load, vanilla lip-sync plays and the settings page identifies the problem. Restart Skyrim after changing this option. See GPU-SETUP.txt.

plugin.name: GPU 0 (default)
plugin.description: Use the default DXGI GPU (index 0) for Audio2Face. Devices are selected independently. The installer cannot detect hardware; choose a GPU by name in the optional in-game menu.

plugin.description: Use DXGI GPU 1 for Audio2Face, independently of Audio2Emotion. Choose only if you know the intended adapter index. An unavailable adapter reports an error; it does not select another GPU.

plugin.name: V3 — full facial detail (recommended)
plugin.description: Most expressive model; detailed lip-sync at 60 fps. Approximately 250 MB GPU memory. Women use Claire; men use Mark. Faster than Legacy in local RTX 4070 tests; speed and memory vary with system and dialogue.

plugin.name: Performance — V3-trained, experimental
plugin.description: 4M-parameter student trained to reproduce V3's answers on familiar dialogue, with per-line memory. Unfamiliar dialogue can be less reliable. 30 fps; no speech-driven eye movement. More computation than Ultra Performance. GPU or CPU; not yet verified on Steam Deck. Speaker coverage is selected separately.

plugin.name: Ultra Performance — lowest computation, experimental
plugin.description: The original 80,729-parameter Performance model, retained under a new name. Lowest computation cost, with less facial detail and less accurate lip-sync, especially on unfamiliar dialogue. 30 fps; no speech-driven eye movement. GPU or CPU. Speaker coverage is selected separately.

plugin.name: Legacy — Audio2Face v2.3
plugin.description: Older facial style at 30 fps with one shared identity. Approximately 100 MB GPU memory. Uses less memory than V3 but is slower in local RTX 4070 tests.

plugin.name: Disabled — vanilla facial animation
plugin.description: Keep vanilla facial animation and skip both inference models. Your Audio2Emotion choice is remembered for later. Re-enable through the installer, INI or optional in-game menu.

plugin.name: Performance (~40 MB VRAM, recommended, experimental)
plugin.description: Estimated additional VRAM usage is about 40 MB on a shared GPU device. Actual usage varies by driver and device mode. Included in both downloads. Small model trained to approximate Full on Skyrim dialogue; unfamiliar quest-mod lines may be hit or miss. The model file is 21.6 MB on disk. Independent of vanilla emotion cues.

plugin.name: Full — broader dialogue coverage
plugin.description: Included only in the with-sentiment download. Original Audio2Emotion model; use for unfamiliar dialogue. Typically adds about 600 MB GPU memory and substantial generation time. CPU uses system memory and extra processing. Independent of vanilla emotion cues.

plugin.name: Disabled — no extra emotion inference
plugin.description: Skip Audio2Emotion to reduce CPU/GPU work and memory use. Audio2Face lip-sync continues. Vanilla / scene emotion cues can remain enabled independently.

plugin.name: Use vanilla / scene emotion cues
plugin.description: Pass authored dialogue emotions, including dialogue-mod inputs, to Audio2Face. Uncheck to remove those inputs. Audio2Emotion is separate; disabling both keeps audio-driven lip-sync. No SKSE settings menu is required.

plugin.name: Active dialogue only — Potato Mode
plugin.description: Animate only the NPC in your active conversation and supported player dialogue. Other speakers keep vanilla animation. Reduces background work; models stay loaded while facial animation is enabled. Uncheck to process all supported speakers.

plugin.name: Animate player dialogue
plugin.description: Animate the player with DBReV 1.4.4+ or experimental DBVO 2 support. Uncheck to keep the voice mod's own player animation and skip BFA player processing. NPCs are unaffected; also applies in active-dialogue-only mode.

plugin.name: Prepare dialogue early
plugin.description: Begin generation when a response is created, before the actor speaks. Can reduce late animation but may process responses never spoken. Uncheck to begin preparation later.

group.name: Beast races — uncheck to keep vanilla animation

plugin.name: Animate ordinary Khajiit
plugin.description: Enable Skyrim Khajiit and Khajiit vampire races. Custom races keep their own defaults; Alfiq remains disabled by default. Individual custom races can be configured in the INI or optional Races menu.

plugin.name: Animate Argonians
plugin.description: Enable Skyrim Argonian and Argonian vampire races. Uncheck if you prefer vanilla animation on these heads. Custom races keep their own defaults.

plugin.name: Tongue animation
plugin.description: Use the current tongue blend with reduced, overlap-limited speech cues. Uncheck to restore the tongue behavior from before this feature; this does not remove the tongue mesh.

plugin.name: Improved eye gaze
plugin.description: The NPC you talk to looks at you, and may look away in the pauses of a line by emotion, onto nearby objects. Works with every facial model; V3 and Old also add small speech-driven eye movement. SE/AE only. Not compatible with The Fourth Wall. Uncheck to keep the game's eye movement and head tracking.

plugin.name: Log generated and played lines
plugin.description: Write bounded dialogue diagnostics to BetterFacialAnimations.log for troubleshooting. Uncheck to reduce routine logging; essential GPU and model errors are still reported. Detailed experimental tracing stays off.

plugin.name: Settings without an in-game menu
plugin.description: These choices work without SKSE Menu Framework. For later edits, use Data/SKSE/Plugins/BetterFacialAnimations.ini and restart Skyrim, or reinstall. The optional menu saves changes automatically. Explicit values in an existing INI override installer defaults. Back up custom settings before reinstalling; check MO2 Overwrite for a winning INI and deploy changes in Vortex. Fine strength, timing, emotion limits and individual NPC/race overrides stay in the INI/menu.

plugin.name: Recover from a GPU hang or crash
plugin.description: Close Skyrim, then reinstall with CPU for both Audio2Face and Audio2Emotion. Or set ForceCPU=1 and EmotionDevice=-1 in the existing [General] section of the winning INI. Do not add duplicate keys. For lower CPU cost, choose Performance facial animation, Disabled emotion and Active dialogue only. CPU runs only when explicitly selected; no new save is needed. Read Data/SKSE/Plugins/BetterFacialAnimations/GPU-SETUP.txt for driver requirements and GPU recovery steps.
